fields.value: The paper frames the relevant behavior as attention control, person attention/tracking, and gaze-direction classification for identifying an addressee. It does not give a standalone definition of robotic gaze or robotic gaze-based attention.

quotes.text: For a successful interaction, the basis of our system is constituted by a robust and continuous tracking of possible communication partners and an attention control for interacting, not only with one person like in the object demonstration but with multiple persons enabling us to also deploy the robot for, e.g., receptionist tasks.

The gazing direction is evaluated for activating or deactivating the speech processing, since the robot should not react to people talking to each other in front of the robot, but only to communication partners facing the robot.

fields.value: Human gaze direction helps select the person addressing the robot and suppresses responses to people conversing with each other. Robot attention also shifts between a person and a referred object, supporting object demonstration and joint attention.

Receiving the according command via the dialog, e.g., “This is an orange cup” in combination with a deictic gesture, the robot’s attention switches from its communication partner to the referred object.
In return, the presented robot is able to perform pointing gestures to presented objects itself, thus achieving joint attention easily (see Fig. 10).

fields.value: Autonomous real-time perception and attention: two eye cameras detect faces and classify horizontal face/gaze direction in 20° steps; two microphones and SPLOC estimate one or more sound-source directions. Face detections validate sound sources; memory-based tracking preserves trusted, stationary people temporarily outside view. The system combines reactive tracking and deliberative dialog through a three-layer hybrid architecture and XML-based module communication.

quotes.text: The eyes are vertically aligned and horizontally steerable autonomously for spatial fixations.

As an extension to the frontal view detection proposed by Viola and Jones, we additionally classify the horizontal gazing direction of faces, as shown in Fig. 4, by using four instances of the classifier pyramids described earlier, trained for faces rotated by 20◦, 40◦, 60◦, and 80◦.
For multiple sound source detection, not only the main energy value of the CSP result is taken, but also all values exceeding an adjustable threshold.
If a person is trusted and not moving, the memory will keep the person’s position and return to it later according to the attention system.

fields.value: BARTHOC is an anthropomorphic humanoid torso robot, about adult-sized from the waist up, with a movable head, facial-expression actuators, two eye cameras, arms, and five-finger hands; two shoulder-mounted microphones support speech and speaker-direction detection.

quotes.text: BARTHOC is able to move its upper body like a sitting human and corresponds to an adult person with a size of 75 cm from its waist upwards.
To achieve human-like FEs, 10 DOFs are used in its face to control jaw, mouth angles, eyes, eye brows, and eye lids.
Each eye contains a FireWire color video camera with a resolution of 640 480 pixels.
For speech understanding and the detection of multiple speaker directions, two microphones are used, one fixed on each shoulder element as a temporary solution.

fields.value: The authors state that anthropomorphic appearance and human-like sensors were chosen to support intuitive understanding and human-like interaction; they also note that appearance affects how people behave toward robots. The paper does not report a comparison isolating embodiment effects in the multiparty attention study.

quotes.text: To foster a better and more intuitive understanding of the system, we propose a strong perception–production relation realized once by human-like sensors as video cameras integrated in the eyes and two mono-microphones, and sec- ondly, by a human-like outward appearance and the ability of showing facial expressions (FEs) and gestures as well.

Regarding the observation that the way humans interact with each other in a teaching task strongly depends on the expectations they have regarding their communication partner, the outward appearance of the robot, and its interaction behavior are adopted inspired by [3], e.g., adults showing objects or demonstrating actions to children act differently from adults interacting with adults.

fields.value: This paper presents BARTHOC, an anthropomorphic robot with autonomous gaze-direction classification, speaker localization, and memory-based tracking for attention to multiple people. In tests, it usually responded to the intended addressee and rarely disturbed people talking to one another; the paper also reports better ratings for emotional mimicry than neutral responses.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5; RQ6 — The paper describes gaze-direction classification and attention control, their role in addressee selection and object-directed joint attention, and reports technical performance and interaction effects. It details sensing and control implementation and BARTHOC’s anthropomorphic embodiment, while discussing how appearance and human-like sensors motivated the system; it does not experimentally isolate embodiment effects.
